input: Need to pick up dry cleaning before Friday.
expected_behavior: Recover the single task as one bullet. Do not split it into multiple bullets or pad with invented related content to reach a higher count.
notes: Draft acceptance case for PROMPT_CONTRACT_VERSION=source-determined-bullets-v1 -- floor case, single supported idea. Has no prior passing baseline, so status is acceptance_gate, not regression_guard -- report_benchmark.py must not describe an initial pass/fail here as a 'regression.' required_semantic_dimensions added per review: without it, a result with every score left null would still count as passing, since a null score isn't rejected the way a wrong score is.

input: Call the dentist to reschedule, and separately, remember to water the plants while I'm away.
expected_behavior: Recover exactly two independent bullets -- one per supported idea -- without merging them into one or splitting either into extra bullets.
notes: Draft acceptance case -- two clearly separable ideas, tests neither merge nor split.

input: Three things: renew the car registration, email a coworker about the project timeline, and pick a paint color for the hallway.
expected_behavior: Recover exactly three bullets, one per stated item, in any order. No fourth bullet invented, no two items merged into one.
notes: Draft acceptance case -- mid-range count, explicitly enumerated by the note itself. Revised to remove a proper name (was 'Sam') per review feedback, reducing accidental overlap with other benchmark fixtures' cast of names.

input: So much going on: the roof needs inspecting, the car needs an oil change, I owe a friend a call back, the gutters are clogged, I still haven't filed the insurance claim, the dog needs a vet visit, I need to return a borrowed drill, and I never finished setting up the new router.
expected_behavior: Use no more than seven bullet lines even though eight distinct supported ideas are present -- the cap is a hard ceiling, not a suggestion. Do not merge two independent ideas into one bullet just to fit under the cap. All eight ideas are explicit tasks and must appear as exactly eight action items, even though at most seven may also appear as their own bullet line. Do not invent a ninth idea, and do not silently drop any of the eight from the action items.
notes: Draft acceptance case -- ceiling case, 8 source ideas against the 7-line cap. Revised per review feedback: removed a proper name that collided with an existing protected probe (was 'Priya', already used in gold_v1.2.1_probes.jsonl probe 05); changed the bullet rule from exact-7 to max-7 (the prior wording self-contradicted by saying 'at most seven' while requiring exactly seven); and, per the latest review, replaced the vague 'survive somewhere in the output' requirement with an explicit action_count_rule of exactly 8 -- all eight ideas here are genuine tasks, so this is objectively checkable via the action_items count instead of requiring subjective judgment about whether an idea 'survived.'

input: Call the insurance company about the claim before Friday. Don't let me forget -- I need to ring up the insurance company about that same claim.
expected_behavior: Recover exactly one task -- call the insurance company about the claim, with the before-Friday deadline preserved -- as one bullet and one action item, even though it is stated twice in different wording. The before-Friday deadline is explicitly supported by the source and must survive somewhere in the output; do not let it quietly disappear. Do not produce two bullets or two action items for what is one restated task; that would be padding via repetition, not two supported ideas. Do not add a second fact, qualifier, or emotional reaction beyond what the source states.
notes: Draft acceptance case -- tests 'never repeat content to reach a target count' specifically. Revised per review feedback: the prior version used two emotional statements with slightly different information (a factual worry vs. a stress reaction), making one-vs-two ideas genuinely debatable. Replaced with one literal, concrete task restated in different wording, removing that ambiguity, and added an explicit action_count_rule since the same restated-task risk applies to action_items, not just bullets. Latest review: added an explicit requirement that the supported 'before Friday' deadline survives, plus a DEADLINE_SURVIVED check -- otherwise the expected_behavior text could be read as permitting that qualifier to quietly disappear as long as the core task remains.
